name: West Street (Xijie) and Town Center
tagline: The neon-lit backpacker heart of Yangshuo
description: The historic pedestrian strip and surrounding town core, packed with bars, cafes, hostels, climbing shops, and street food. It is touristy and lively, easy to meet people, and central to everything, but noise and crowds are the trade-off for staying in the thick of it.
bestFor: Backpackers and social solo travelers who want nightlife and convenience
pros: Walkable to bars, cafes, and shops
cons: Noisy and crowded, especially at night

name: Yulong River Valley
tagline: Countryside guesthouses among the karst peaks
description: A rural spread of villages, rice paddies, and boutique riverside guesthouses west of town along the gentle Yulong River. It is peaceful and photogenic, perfect for cycling and slow mornings, though you will rely on a bike, scooter, or transfers to reach the town center.
bestFor: Nomads and couples wanting calm, nature, and space to focus
cons: Far from town amenities and nightlife
Needs a bike or scooter to get around

name: Xingping
description: An old riverside town upstream on the Li River, home to the famous viewpoint printed on the 20-yuan note. It is more traditional and slower than Yangshuo proper, with heritage streets and cruise-boat access, ideal for a scenic riverside base away from the main tourist churn.
bestFor: Photographers and travelers seeking a quieter, scenic riverside stay
cons: Limited services compared with Yangshuo town
Roughly an hour from central Yangshuo

name: Gaotian and the Guilin Road Countryside
tagline: Quiet farmland gateway to the peaks
description: A rural township south of Yangshuo near Moon Hill and the road toward Guilin, surrounded by farmland and climbing crags. It is unhurried and cheap, popular with rock climbers and travelers who prize quiet over convenience, with the town a short bus or scooter ride away.
bestFor: Rock climbers and budget travelers wanting peace near the crags
pros: Close to Moon Hill and climbing areas
